items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: So he asked me if I would like to join his band. I didn’t even know who he was. And I told him yes.

ctx.x: Let me ask you, how did you get the nickname “Panama?”

I’ve been asked that so many times. I wish I had a dollar for every time I’ve been asked that. What happened, I joined Roy Eldridge. In fact I met Roy at a jam session, ‘cause as I say I was very competitive and I used to go looking for jam sessions. And so I went to this jam session and Roy Eldridge heard me. And he liked the way that I played behind him. And his drummer was leaving the band to join Chic Webb’s band because Chic was in the hospital. He hadn’t died yet but he left to join Chic’s band. And so Roy…

Glaser walks in. And he asked for Big Sid. So Roy said “I don’t know where he is.” So he said “well who is that setting up the drums there?” And without batting an eye, he just turned around and said “oh, that’s Panama” ‘cause I had on a Panama hat. It was the summertime and I had just come from Florida, and that was the style in Florida, a Panama hat. So I had on a Panama hat. And I was too scared to tell the fellows, you know here I am in the big league now. Too scared to tell the guys that my name was David.…

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: But I had this job lined up with Roy Eldridge, and so I joined his band

ctx.x: But I had this job lined up with Roy Eldridge, and so I joined his band, like, the first week in

July, and that's when my name was changed from David to Panama. That's the reason when I meet someone that calls me David right now, it's someone that knew me before 1939. You know, you can always tell the people who knew me before 1939, because they would call me David, with the exception of a few musicians, one outstanding, and that's my boy, Binks "Dizzy" Gillespie; he calls me David, and he never called me Panama.

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: And the next night, Panama was there; Zutty didn't show no more.

ctx.x: So I said to myself, "I'm not gonna get in no argument with this cat. I told Slam, I said, "When we go back on, we're not going on the bandstand." I said, "Just bring the bass and follow me." I went to the bar, and Slam played at the bar, and then we played to the tables until the set was over. We did that the next set, and he got the message then. I wasn't about be playing with him (?), you know. And the next night, Panama was there; Zutty didn't show no more.
Well, I had no choice, man! And I liked Zutty, you know. But he just...
